A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RegMean++ research work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison despite substantial expansion and reorganization in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original vision and language model-merging experiments, including benchmark accuracy, sequential merging, robustness, ablations and computational measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds CKA analyses, expanded language-model comparisons, computational measurements and failure examples.

M1.justification: Both versions use previous merged-layer activations, regularized inner-product matrices, the same closed-form merging solution and averaging for other parameters. v3 expands Algorithm 1 to explicitly show candidate-layer forward passes and matrix construction, clarifying the existing procedure.

E1.justification: v3 newly reports validation coverage using MMLU STEM subjects, LAMBADA, CoNaLa and WildJailbreak, alongside reused IFEval (Appendix B.1). The original 20 vision tasks, 11 language evaluation datasets and four multilingual evaluation languages are retained. Added Gemma models change model configurations rather than task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 6 adds Model Soups, Task Arithmetic and TIES-Merging to the Llama comparisons, which previously compared only RegMean and RegMean++. Sequential comparisons for ViT-B/16 and ViT-L/14 expand from that pair to the full merger set. CKA comparisons also introduce multi-task learning as a reference for two architectures.

E3.justification: New evaluation settings include Gemma-2-2B and Gemma-2-9B, cross-layer and intra-layer minibatch CKA, and language-model and layer-subset timing protocols. The added language baselines receive method-specific hyperparameter searches. Existing vision task sequences and the RegMean language calibration budget and scaling-factor grid are retained.

E4.justification: v3 replaces the nonlinear-component bias curves with broader CKA analyses while retaining the final-layer representation-bias analysis. It adds layer-subset timing diagnostics in Table 18 and high-alpha language failure examples in Figures 19–20. Existing corruption, layer/component accuracy and data-characteristic analyses largely remain.

E5.justification: Appendix D.10 adds explicit standard deviations for sequential merging, OOD generalization and class imbalance, where v2 reported five-run means without numerical dispersion. Appendix C.4 specifies unbiased minibatch HSIC estimation and ten dataset passes for CKA. The original five-run counts are retained; an increase in those runs is not established.

E6.justification: Core vision Table 1 values remain unchanged, but Table 5 changes RegMean++'s ViT-B/32 class-imbalance score from 76.5 to 76.3. Table 6 revises its Llama-3.2-3B average from 33.0 to 31.9 and RegMean's Llama-3.1-8B average from 44.8 to 43.5. Sequential heatmap values also change. Added Gemma, baseline, CKA, timing and failure results substantially expand the evidence; the language revisions do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The original regularized objective and Appendix A derivation remain unchanged. v3 adds a cubic-in-width, linear-in-depth computational scaling argument in Appendix D.9, and specifies CKA/HSIC definitions and invariance properties in Appendix C.4. These are limited formal additions.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution summary narrow the performance claim from competitive or state-of-the-art results to competitive performance. The central contribution of incorporating layer dependencies and the main generalization, robustness and sequential-merging claims remain.

C2.justification: Beyond v2's existing language-performance caveats, v3 discusses cases where data-free alternatives are more accurate and efficient, and adds Gemma results that qualify model-scale generalization. Appendices D.8–D.9 explain I/O and memory effects, high-alpha gibberish and computational bottlenecks. Appendix E proposes selective hybrid merging to reduce overhead.

D1.justification: v3 supplies language validation datasets, selected hyperparameters, baseline search grids, batch size, and additional checkpoint and data access references. It newly specifies the vision validation fraction, CKA implementation settings, and language-model loading and CPU-offloading procedures. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation without establishing changes to every previously reported setting.

R1.justification: Related work adds Daheim et al.'s gradient-matching approach, while new references support CKA/HSIC, Gemma and validation datasets. The main positioning relative to RegMean and existing merging approaches is retained. Publication updates to works such as FusionBench and MergeBench are bibliographic changes rather than new cited research.

P1.justification: v3 broadly copyedits the abstract, introduction, method and results. It separates Preliminaries from Related Work, moves Related Work after the experiments, swaps the OOD and robustness subsections, and reorganizes the appendices with a contents page and clearer experimental-detail subsections.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redrawn with transformer-component detail. New CKA and failure figures, expanded sequential-comparison panels, rearranged heatmaps, and additional result, uncertainty and timing tables materially change presentation. Journal typesetting and table placement also reshape the layout; several existing appendix plots are retained or relocated.

improvement.justification: v3 resolves important gaps in comparative evidence and reporting. The language study adds competitive data-free baselines and Gemma models, exposing limits that the earlier RegMean-only comparison could not establish. Explicit CKA procedures, standard deviations, implementation details, costs and failure examples substantially improve assessability and reproducibility, while the headline performance claim is moderated. IFEval's disclosed reuse for validation and evaluation remains a limitation, but the overall quality gain is clear.
